item.title: Educating Traumatized Teenagers: The Extraordinary Story of a Swedish International School
item.description:
Thursday, July 16, 2026 at 6:30 PM

After World War II, Sweden absorbed and provided medical treatment for thousands of sick survivors. What to do about those who were teenagers, who had missed years of study on account of the war? In September 1945, the Swedish government issued an order for schooling to be offered to those under the age of 18. In this presentation, Dr. Bernice Lerner will describe the complex process of recruiting wary adolescents, the challenges of teaching homeless, orphaned, and “environmentally damaged” teenagers, and instructors’ goals and methods at the most experimental of sites—the “Internat” school her mother attended. Dr. Bernice Lerner is the author of All the Horrors of War: A Jewish Girl, a British Doctor, and the Liberation of Bergen-Belsen, and other writings on the Holocaust and on virtue ethics. She is the former dean of adult learning at Hebrew College, former lecturer on the Holocaust at Boston University, and a senior scholar at Boston University’s Center for Character and Social Responsibility. Gerald S. Kaplan Endowed Lecture.

From Holocaust Museum Houston

This post contains affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Official Tickets Resale Tickets Comedy Cellar Las Vegas brings one of the most legendary names in stand-up comedy to the heart of Las Vegas. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

item.title: Mapping Houston's Innovation Ecosystem
item.description:
Friday, July 17, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Ion – Conference Room 027, 4201 Main St, Houston, TX, 77002

Facilitated by Wade Pinder, Ion’s Mentor in Residence Houston’s startup and innovation ecosystem is as vast and dynamic as the city itself, full of opportunities, resources, and talent. Yet, navigating it can be challenging—especially for those unfamiliar with its many parts. Whether you’re an entrepreneur, investor, educator, student, community leader or curious professional, this session will offer valuable insights into how Houston’s innovation ecosystem works and how you can find your place within it. Discover the Houston Ecosystem’s Flow Facilitated by Wade Pinder, the Ion’s Mentor in Residence, this session will help participants map out the journey needed to take an idea from concept to a mature company. Wade brings years of experience in product management, community building, and mentoring entrepreneurs to the table, offering a thoughtful and informed perspective to guide this exploration. The heart of the session lies in exploring a dynamic mind map that Wade has created and continues to refine—an ever-evolving, community-driven tool that grows alongside Houston’s innovation ecosystem. Attendees will not only learn about the ecosystem’s flow but also have the opportunity to contribute to it by identifying gaps, sharing knowledge, and adding their insights. This session will center on the stages of a company’s growth journey, exploring the essential elements that drive it forward. Participants will examine the role of financial capital, from early fundraising efforts to securing the resources needed for scaling, and how these milestones align with a company’s progression. The discussion will also delve into the human element of growing a business, highlighting the evolving talent and expertise required to navigate the entrepreneurial journey. Additionally, we’ll explore the importance of “social capital”—the networks, support systems, and relationships that play a critical role in moving ideas to market and sustaining long-term growth. Ion’s Vision Helping the community better understand the local ecosystem reflects the Ion’s commitment “to being the home for Houston’s innovation community.” By fostering connections, creating opportunities, and sharing perspectives, the Ion is building a transformative culture that strengthens Houston’s economic resiliency and celebrates the entrepreneurial journey. From forming an initial entrepreneurial idea to the prototyping phase to scaling a business, this Houston Ecosystem Mapping session aligns with the Ion’s goals to support innovation, attract talent, and build a vibrant ecosystem. Who Should Attend? This session is ideal for: Entrepreneurs looking to understand greater Houston’s resources. Investors curious about the local startup landscape. Professionals and students wanting to connect with the innovation community. Anyone passionate about Houston’s growth as a hub for innovation and entrepreneurship. Innovators who have recently moved to greater Houston and are looking to get “plugged in” to the local scene. Community leaders and service providers that support (or want to support) the innovation ecosystem. Event Details 📅 Date:  Friday, March 21, 2025 ⏰ Time:  10:00am 📍 Location:  The Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX Register today for this chance to explore Houston’s ecosystem, uncover its flow, and help shape its future.

item.title: Cobalt Photocatalysis as a Platform for Tunable Hydrogen Atom Transfer in the Ring Opening of Cyclic Ethers
item.description:
Friday, July 17, 2026 at 8 PM

Location: BioScience Research Collaborative

  Speaker: Brian Funk Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Chemistry Location: BioScience Research Collaborative 1060 A/B This dissertation explores thoughtful design and development of synthetic methods photocatalyzed by Vitamin B12 and analogous cobaloximes. Central to these protocols is control over diverging HAT from Earth-abundant Cobalt complexes and simple organic thiols, shown to be heavily influenced by proticity of the reaction environment. Through strategic control of HAT directionality, these works provide mild, complementary reactive scaffolds to classical hydrogenation by hydride nucleophiles and carbonyl production by traditional Meinwald rearrangements. The addition of these new techniques to the synthetic chemist's toolbox has the potential to improve the limited accessibility of hydride-like reactivity in chemical synthesis, influence the perception of cyclic ethers as precursors to valuable functional handles, and further advance the onset of VB12 and its derivatives as powerful photocatalysts. Armed with the strong mechanistic foundation elucidated throughout this dissertation, further application of Cobalt photocatalysis in broader substrate classes can maximize the impact of this powerful, sustainable, and tunable reactivity.   (Department : Chemistry)

From Rice University - Open to the Public

His comedy is raw, honest, and deeply rooted in the American experience, resonating with audiences who appreciate comedy that doesn’t pull its punches. Gillis gained national attention through his podcast “Matt and Shane’s Secret Podcast” and his stand-up specials, including “Live in Austin” and “Beautiful Dogs” on Netflix. He returned to Saturday Night Live as a host in 2024 to massive acclaim, cementing his status as one of the defining comedic voices of his generation. This Lincoln Financial Field show is a homecoming of sorts — Gillis performing in his home state of Pennsylvania for one of the biggest comedy events the city has ever seen. Located at 1 Lincoln Financial Field Way in South Philadelphia, the stadium holds approximately 69,000 fans and offers a world-class entertainment experience at every level. The Linc features multiple concourse levels with food and beverage options, premium club spaces, luxury suites, and state-of-the-art sound and lighting systems. Parking is available in the stadium’s surrounding lots (advance purchase recommended for major events). The venue is accessible via SEPTA’s Broad Street Line (AT&T Station) and by car via I-95 and I-76. This is a massive event — plan to arrive early and enjoy the full stadium atmosphere. What to Expect This is not just a comedy show — it’s a historic event. Shane Gillis performing at Lincoln Financial Field represents one of the largest stand-up comedy shows ever staged in Philadelphia. Expect a full evening of Gillis’s signature brand of comedy, joined by a lineup of special guests that promises to make this an unforgettable night. Official Tickets Resale Tickets Comedy Cellar Las Vegas brings one of the most legendary names in stand-up comedy to the heart of Las Vegas. Located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino, this intimate comedy club is the West Coast home of New York City’s world-famous Comedy Cellar, the venue that helped launch the careers of comedy icons including Dave Chappelle, Chris Rock, Jon Stewart, Ray Romano, Amy Schumer, Aziz Ansari, and countless others. Unlike traditional comedy shows featuring a single headliner, Comedy Cellar presents a carefully curated lineup of professional comedians every night. Audiences can expect multiple performers during each show, featuring a mix of nationally touring headliners, television favorites, Comedy Central veterans, Netflix performers, and rising stars from around the world. No two shows are exactly alike, making every visit a unique experience. Surprise drop-in appearances from major comedians performing elsewhere in Las Vegas have become part of the club’s reputation, giving audiences the chance to see comedy superstars in an intimate setting. Event Details Venue: Comedy Cellar Las Vegas at Rio Hotel & Casino Location: 3700 W Flamingo Rd, Las Vegas, NV 89103 Show Schedule: Nightly performances throughout the year Age Requirement: Recommended for audiences 18+ due to mature comedy content About the Venue Opened in 2018, Comedy Cellar Las Vegas was designed to recreate the atmosphere and energy of the original Greenwich Village club that has become one of the most respected comedy venues in the world. The 300-seat showroom offers excellent sightlines and an intimate setting that allows audiences to experience stand-up comedy exactly as it was meant to be seen: up close and personal. The venue combines the excitement of a Las Vegas night out with the authentic feel of a classic New York comedy club. Guests can enjoy a comfortable showroom environment while watching some of the best comedians working today perform in a setting that encourages spontaneity, crowd interaction, and unforgettable moments. Conveniently located inside the Rio Hotel & Casino just minutes from the Las Vegas Strip, the venue offers easy access for both tourists and local comedy fans. What to Expect Expect a fast-paced evening featuring multiple comedians performing throughout the show. The Comedy Cellar is known for showcasing a wide variety of comedic styles, from observational humor and storytelling to sharp social commentary, crowd work, and cutting-edge stand-up. Whether you’re discovering a future comedy star or watching a seasoned veteran perfect their craft, every show delivers the authentic comedy club experience that has made the Comedy Cellar one of the most respected brands in stand-up comedy. For comedy fans visiting Las Vegas, Comedy Cellar is widely considered one of the best places in the city to experience live stand-up comedy any night of the week.

His stand-up is deeply personal, brutally honest, and darkly funny — exploring themes of anxiety, addiction, relationships, and the absurdity of modern life. Maron has released several acclaimed Netflix specials including Too Real, End Times Fun, and From Bleak to Dark, each showcasing his evolution as a storyteller and comedian. The Yammering into the Void Tour promises all-new material from one of comedy’s most authentic and compelling voices. If you appreciate comedy that makes you think as much as it makes you laugh, this is the show for you. Event Details Date: Saturday, July 18, 2026 Doors: 6:00 PM | Show Time: 7:00 PM Venue: Rialto Theatre, 318 Congress St, Tucson, AZ 85701 Ticket Price Range: $61 – $364 Age Restrictions: All ages welcome About the Venue The Rialto Theatre is one of Tucson’s most beloved and historic entertainment venues, located in the vibrant downtown arts district on Congress Street. Originally built in 1920, the Rialto has been beautifully restored and now serves as a premier mid-size venue with a capacity of approximately 1,300 guests. The venue features a general admission floor area, reserved balcony seating, and excellent acoustics that make every performance feel intimate and immersive. The Rialto’s historic architecture — with its ornate details and warm lighting — creates a truly special atmosphere for live comedy and music events. Street parking and nearby parking garages are available in the downtown area. The venue is surrounded by great restaurants and bars, making it easy to turn the evening into a full night out in Tucson’s lively downtown scene. What to Expect Marc Maron’s Yammering into the Void Tour is a solo stand-up performance featuring brand-new material. Expect Maron’s signature stream-of-consciousness storytelling, sharp cultural observations, and deeply personal confessions delivered with his trademark intensity and wit. The show runs approximately 75–90 minutes. Maron’s performances are known for their conversational intimacy — even in a packed venue, it feels like he’s talking directly to you. This is a rare opportunity to see one of comedy’s most respected voices perform live in an intimate setting. Doors open at 6:00 PM. Arrive early to grab a drink at the bar and soak in the Rialto’s historic atmosphere before the show. Ticket Information Tickets range from $61 to $364 depending on seat location. item.title: Essays on Market Design, Complementarities, and Technology Adoption
item.description:
Monday, July 20, 2026 at 3 PM

Location: Kraft

  Speaker: Jingyun Huang Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Economics This dissertation studies how allocation is shaped by complementarities, participation frictions, and the design of market institutions. The chapters examine settings in which agents make choices over related objects or technologies: highway contracts sold sequentially within a day, spectrum licenses sold through a simultaneous clock auction, and consumer-facing generative AI tools adopted across countries. Across these settings, the dissertation asks how observed choices reveal economic primitives, and how market outcomes change when agents face constraints on entry, capacity, information, or access. The first chapter studies sequential highway procurement auctions in Oklahoma. Morning and afternoon contracts are sold on the same day, allowing early awards to affect later entry and bidding. I estimate a structural model that separates standalone costs, cost synergies, fixed entry costs, and firm-day capacity constraints. The estimates show that small firms obtain larger proportional cost savings from same-day project synergies, but higher participation barriers limit their ability to act on these gains. Counterfactuals comparing sequential auctions, simultaneous unbundled auctions, and targeted bundling show that auction format affects both procurement spending and the distribution of awards across firms. The second chapter studies FCC Auction 110, a 5G spectrum auction in which bidders may value combinations of geographic markets. I use a revealed-preference approach to construct moment inequalities from clock-phase bidding choices and recover bounds on standalone values and geographic complementarities. The estimates support positive complementarities across markets. Counterfactual reallocations indicate that locally supported changes can raise value, though the welfare conclusions remain bounded rather than point identified. The third chapter measures global adoption of consumer-facing generative AI tools using high-frequency website traffic data from Semrush. The chapter documents rapid entry, persistent ChatGPT dominance, accelerating usage, widening adoption gaps between high- and low-income countries, and strong home-market advantages for non-U.S. tools. Together, the chapters show that allocation in modern markets depends not only on preferences and costs, but also on the institutional and technological conditions that determine who can act on them.  https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/3813885532?pwd=OGhoVU1aVnRCR2k5STZXTk5CZzFlZz09&omn=95611363587 (https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/3813885532?pwd=OGhoVU1aVnRCR2k5STZXTk5CZzFlZz09&omn=95611363587) (Department : Economics)

item.title: Angel Investing 101
item.description:
Tuesday, July 21, 2026 at 5:30 PM

Location: Ion – Conference Room 029 – 030, 4201 Main St, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Register here: https://luma.com/w1itcerp In a world where only the very wealthy, well connected, and major institutions have access to premium investment opportunities, which have created massive wealth for a small portion of the population, the Innovation Center for Urban Entrepreneurship team believes the key to closing income and wealth gaps globally is to democratize access to opportunities across the investment ecosystem. Join the Innovation Center for Urban Entrepreneurship team for an evening of learning, discussion and possibilities as we explore the basics of angel investing and the role it plays in bringing new products and services to market and the impact it has on wealth and job creation.. At this event, you’ll learn the key components to successfully navigate the critical-path of investing in private, early-stage companies. This session is ideal for the following investment related stakeholders: Prospective Angel Investors who want to learn more about the world of Angel Investing Investment Advisors (RIA/FA) who are looking for alternative investments for their clients Entrepreneurs who want to learn more about what Angels are looking for in their deals Entrepreneurs who want to meet/network with Angel Investors Ion District Investor Activation Program: The Houston Ion District Investor Activation Program along with Urban Capital Network is helping build an equitable climatetech industry capable of rapid deployment by addressing a fundamental challenge: the region’s lack of funding for early-stage climatetech startups, and especially for those led by underrepresented founders. This program from Greentown Labs and the Ion brings early-stage investors from Greater Houston—a region playing a pivotal role in the energy transition—into the fold, offering education on climatetech investing, channeling a pool of capital to young startups, and catalyzing a thriving climatetech investment ecosystem that prioritizes diversity, equity, and inclusion. If you would like to join the program, please fill out this form, and if you have additional questions, please contact Juliana Bernal Martinez at jbernal@greentownlabs.com.

item.title: VEGA: A Computational Theory of Visual Grouping
item.description:
Tuesday, July 21, 2026 at 8 PM

Location: Kraft Hall

  Speaker: Shrreya Aagarwal Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Psychology Location: Kraft Hall 110 Information organization is fundamental to how humans interact with and perceive the world. Understanding how humans naturally group interface elements is therefore essential for designing intuitive user experiences; effective grouping helps users find information more efficiently, reducing search time and frustration. Previous work in this domain has either prioritized proximity or tested Gestalt principles in isolation–this work builds a grouping hierarchy from the ground up by pitting principles directly against one another. The present work focuses on understanding users' preferred grouping (rows, columns, or neutral) when Gestalt principles compete, in order to inform a computational model of visual grouping. A series of experiments tested the effects of and interactions between various Gestalt principles through stimuli arranged in grids that were incrementally manipulated. The experiments reveal a hierarchical nature among the principles: shape similarity and common region emerge as the strongest grouping cues, followed by alignment, with proximity as the weakest. These findings challenge the proximity-first assumptions that have dominated the literature and provide key insights into the mechanisms underlying perceptual grouping. Building on these findings, this research guides the successful development of a computational model capable of predicting users' grouping preferences within a given interface. Furthermore, an additional experiment testing the model's sensitivity across various screen sizes was conducted, ensuring its generalizability to real-world contexts, such as digital ecosystems. Together, this work advances a comprehensive visual grouping theory and offers actionable principles for the design of 2-D interfaces.   (Department : Psychology)

From Rice University - Open to the Public

item.title: Strange Orientations: Forrest Bess and the Texas Gulf Coast
item.description:
Thursday, July 23, 2026 at 2 PM

Location: See Zoom Link

  Speaker: Corey Stout Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Art History In this dissertation, I explore the significance and impact of the Gulf Coast on the work of Texas artist Forrest Bess (1911-1977). Bess, represented by Betty Parsons Gallery in the 1950s and 1960s, moved to the coast to explore visions he had been having since childhood. Although art historians have acknowledged the imagery of the coastal landscape in his paintings, scholarship on Bess has largely centered on his visions and their symbolic meanings. This emphasis has obscured the formative role of the coastal environment, and I argue that the coast was not simply the setting for his exploration of these visions but was a material and conceptual context that shaped his practice. Drawing on his artworks, photographs, correspondence, and archival materials, I demonstrate how his practice emerged through a reciprocal relationship between the body and the coastal environment to produce a queer way of inhabiting space that dissolves the boundaries between the two. I first examine how Bess used modernist abstraction to produce a visual language that folded the body and coastal landscape into one another to explore queer embodiment and subjectivity. I then consider how the material and spatial conditions of the Gulf Coast expanded Bess's practice beyond the canvas to explore architecture, photography, labor, and everyday life as sites of artistic production. Finally, I show that Bess engaged with petroleum and the oil industry along the Texas Gulf Coast as a material framework for understanding the intersection of queerness and madness. By repositioning Bess within the context of the Texas Gulf Coast, I expand our understanding of his artistic practice beyond painting, while also demonstrating how Bess anticipated later developments of performance, conceptual, and environmental art.   https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/2066552633?pwd=KzNsbTRwM0FQQWQrWFFUMXdUMjJRZz09 (Department : Art History)

item.title: NASA Tech Talks: Optimizing Sensorimotor Performance During Space Exploration
item.description:
Thursday, July 23, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: Ion, 4201 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

We want HOU! Join us to discover NASA’s toughest tech challenges—and apply your skills and expertise to solve them. Living in an altered gravity environment, such as microgravity or the lunar surface, drives adaptative changes in how the brain utilizes sensory information to maintain spatial awareness and control of movement. Dr. Scott Wood will describe how these challenges may impact critical mission tasks astronauts are required to complete, and some of the technology that has been developed to optimize their performance while mitigating these sensorimotor risks. The development of assessment and interventional tools has benefitted from clinical developments to support patient populations. The need for more autonomous operations during exploration missions will also motivate future opportunities for technology sharing with terrestrial medicine. Please join us after the talk for drinks and networking at Second Draught! About the Speakers Scott Wood is a neuroscientist for NASA’s Human Health and Performance Directorate at the Johnson Space Center in Houston, TX. He has been the Co-Lead for the Crew Health Countermeasures portfolio for the Mars Campaign Office charged with developing technologies and countermeasures for exploration missions. He is also the Sensorimotor Discipline Lead for the Health and Countermeasures Element with the Human Research Program (HRP). As part of the Neuroscience Laboratory, he has participated in numerous flight studies and supports neurological functional tests used for medical assessments. Dr. Wood began his research career at NASA while completing his doctorate at the Baylor College of Medicine in Houston, TX. In addition to his spaceflight research, he has also conducted research in clinical and military aerospace laboratories. Montgomery B. Goforth   has more than 40 years of experience as both Engineer and Manager in a variety of highly technical space and defense-related efforts.  After working for a small defense contractor specializing in anti-submarine warfare, he joined NASA’s Johnson Space Center in 1990.  He has held leadership positions in multiple JSC Directorates and Program Offices. In his previous role as Assistant Director of the JSC Engineering Directorate, he established a framework to better focus Engineering’s efforts towards Human Spaceflight technology and systems development consistent with JSC and Agency goals for exploration. Mr. Goforth is now serving as Acting Director of the Business Development & Technology Integration Office at JSC, and as the JSC Chief Technologist.  In these capacities he will be helping to expand the Houston Aerospace Community through the identification of opportunities to develop space/terrestrial technologies of interest to JSC and Human Space Exploration.  Mr. Goforth was born in East Texas, raised in Southern California and Arizona, and graduated from Rice University (BSME 1982, MSME 1987). About NASA Tech Talks In these presentations, occurring the fourth Thursdays of the month, Mr. Montgomery Goforth and other aerospace subject matter experts will discuss the technology development challenges faced by NASA’s Johnson Space Center and the surrounding Aerospace community in our ongoing efforts as the hub of human spaceflight. Presentations will focus on the ways in which these challenges, and the associated opportunities, can be leveraged by Houston’s innovation community. We will continue to identify potential space/terrestrial technologies of interest to Human Spaceflight.  Past NASA Tech Talks have included topics such as: From Space to Startup: Leveraging NASA Technology and Innovation to Propel Your Growing Enterprise Disruptive Filter Technology for Spacecraft Water Treatment:  The New Promise of Graphene Lunar dust capture using novel multiplexed inertial filter Lunar Passive Fuel Cell Technologies: Microbes in Space

item.title: Characterization of Young Active Stars for Identifying the Youngest Exoplanets
item.description:
Thursday, July 23, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Brockman Hall for Physics

  Speaker: Shih-Yun Tang Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Physics & Astronomy Location: Brockman Hall for Physics 300 The most direct way to understand planet formation is to study planetary systems in their earliest evolutionary stages. As pre-main-sequence solar analogs, T Tauri stars (TTSs) are captured before and after the epoch of protoplanetary disk dispersal, marking the boundary at which the main planetary migration occurs. However, the intense magnetic activity inherent in these young hosts poses severe challenges for current detection techniques, such as the transit and radial velocity (RV) methods. Strong, localized magnetic fields suppress convective flux across the stellar photosphere, creating extensive starspots that not only contaminate true planetary signals but also introduce substantial biases when characterizing the fundamental parameters of the host stars. Without a robust means to disentangle and characterize these activity signatures, deriving reliable physical parameters necessary to infer planetary properties and constrain planet-formation models remains challenging.   This dissertation is dedicated to developing a model to simulate the effects of starspots on high-resolution stellar spectra and exploring their resulting impacts on key observational diagnostics, including RVs, photometry, and temperature-sensitive spectral lines. The thesis is organized into four primary parts. First, we analyze a young binary system, DI Tau, to demonstrate how magnetic activity compromises our ability to obtain reliable stellar parameters. Second, we calibrate and characterize a set of temperature-sensitive lines in the $H$ band to track short-term and seasonal variations in the apparent effective temperature of active TTSs. Third, we provide a comprehensive description of the development and verification of EXSPLOSYN, a grid-integrated, high-resolution spotted spectral synthesis framework. Finally, we leverage this simulation to forward-model the surface-temperature inhomogeneities of the weak-lined TTS LkCa 4 and found wavelength-dependent agreement between our simulated profiles and empirical datasets, confirming the reported differences in sensitivity to the hot and cool components at different wavelengths. With EXSPLOSYN, we also provided a critical benchmark for the widely used two-template spectral-fitting technique. We found a potential bias in the technique in overestimating spot size by a factor of 2. https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/92151775597?pwd=o0f7BaKC8rAFtoJTmOjaNZxzwEnk7G.1 (Department : Physics & Astronomy)

item.title: Fourth Saturday Phenology Walk
item.description:
Saturday, July 25, 2026 at 9 AM

Fourth Saturday of the Month9:00 – 11:00 amFree, donations appreciatedAll ages, minors must be accompanied by an adult Meet in front of the Nature Center building Discover the hidden seasonal rhythms of nature firsthand on our guided Phenology Walks, where we track the life cycles of different plants across ecosystems, from the first spring bud burst to winter dormancy. You’ll learn how shifting weather patterns and climate change influence the timing of these important events in our local ecosystems and how you can become a community scientist, contributing vital data from your own backyard to a global research initiative. These relaxing morning walks are led by scientists from Rice University and staff from the Arboretum. We welcome nature enthusiasts of all ages, however kids 12 years and younger must be accompanied by a guardian. Learn more about the study of phenology and ways you can contribute at https://www.usanpn.org/nn Community Science Partner

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.title: Houston Museum of Natural Science
item.description:
Sunday, July 26, 2026 at 2 PM

Location: Levy Park (Event Pavilion), TX

The Houston Museum of Natural Science comes to Levy Park to offer an opportunity to learn firsthand from Museum experts. Encounter real specimens and artifacts from the museum collection in an intimate, educational atmosphere. May 31: Rocks and Minerals Explore the fascinating characteristics of the most important building blocks of Earth’s crust. July 26: Energy Exciting demonstrations explore the remarkable forms of energy we encounter every day. August 30: Dinosaur Discovery Peek into the thrilling daily life of the dinosaur: investigate what dinosaurs ate, how they hunted, and the adaptations they developed to survive in a harsh prehistoric world. September 27: Birds Encounter an amazing variety of birds and discover their fascinating ancestral roots, while learning about their adaptations for success. October 25: Ancient Egypt From mummies to the pyramids, experience amazing architectural and cultural aspects of Ancient Egypt. November 29: Little Bodies, Big Jobs! Brings a selection of live arthropods from the Cockrell Butterfly Center to your classroom. Audiences of all ages will have a unique opportunity to meet some of the hardest workers in the invertebrate world up close and personal. December 13:  Astronomy  Investigate our place in space and ways we study this exciting place full of planets, moons, stars, and galaxies.

From Levy Park Houston

item.title: Art + Climate CONVERSATIONS: Emily Johnson
item.description:
Wednesday, July 29, 2026 at 6:30 PM

Location: DiverseWorks – MATCHBOX 2, 3400 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Presented by DW Art + Climate Partners6:30 pm, Wednesday, July 29, 2026Suggested Ticket Price: $25 (pay-what-you-wish) Get Tickets10% of ticket sales will be donated to the Texas Tribal Buffalo Project The DiverseWorks Art + Climate Partners present Emily Johnson as the inaugural speaker for Art + Climate CONVERSATIONS. Join Houstonians, climate advocates, dance and art enthusiasts, and artists alike on the evening of July 29th for a talk by Johnson, a Yup’ik multi-disciplinary artist, choreographer, land and water protector, and organizer for justice, sovereignty and well-being. In October 2026, Johnson’s Overflow Radio will be presented at DiverseWorks. Art + Climate CONVERSATIONS highlights artists and creatives that are leading the way on addressing climate-related issues through their work. The DW Art + Climate Partners support and advise on climate programming and future projects. DiverseWorks’ Art + Climate program began in 2023-24 and consists of a climate action plan that guides the organization; programming that increases awareness of the effects of climate change; support for artists to develop environmentally sustainable practices; and the development of a new, climate-forward facility for artists, community members, and other non-profit organizations to share. Speaker BioEmily Johnson is a Bessie Award-winning choreographer, Guggenheim, Native Arts and Cultures Foundation, and United States Artists Fellow, and recipient of the Doris Duke Artist Award. She is based in Lenapehoking / New York City. Emily is of the Yup’ik Nation, and since 1998 has created work that considers the experience of sensing and seeing performance. Her dances function as portals and care processions, they engage audienceship within and through space, time, and environment — interacting with a place’s architecture, peoples, history and role in building futures. Emily is trying to make a world where performance is part of life; where performance is an integral part of our connection to each other, our environment, our stories, our past, present and future. Her choreography and gatherings have been presented across what is currently called the United States and Australia. Her large-scale project, Then a Cunning Voice and A Night We Spend Gazing at Stars is an all-night outdoor performance gathering taking place amongst 84 community-hand-made quilts. It premiered in Lenapehoking (NYC) in 2017, and was presented in Zhigaagoong (Chicago) in 2019. She choreographed the Santa Fe Opera production of Doctor Atomic, directed by Peter Sellars in 2018. Being Future Being, premiered on Tongva Land in Los Angeles in 2022. In 2011, DiverseWorks presented her performance The Thank-You Bar in conjunction with the exhibition This is Displacement: Native Artists Consider the Relationship Between Land and Identity (co-curated by Johnson and Diné visual artist Carolyn Lee Anderson).  Emily’s writing has been published and commissioned by The Open Society University Network’s Center for Human Rights and the Arts, ArtsLink Australia, unMagazine, Dance Research Journal (University of Cambridge Press); SFMOMA; Transmotion Journal, University of Kent; Movement Research Journal; Pew Center for Arts and Heritage; and the compilation Imagined Theaters: Writing for a Theoretical Stage (Routledge). Emily hosts monthly ceremonial fires on Mannahatta in partnership with Abrons Arts Center and Kai Recollet. She was the Pueblo Opera Cultural Council Diplomat at Santa Fe Opera 2018-2020, and a lead organizer of First Nations Dialogues. She was a co-compiler of the documents, Creating New Futures: Guidelines for Ethics and Equity in the Performing Arts and Notes for Equitable Funding, was a member of Creative Time’s inaugural Think Tank, and serves as a working consortium member for First Nations Performing Arts.

item.title: Ionospheric O⁺ Transport to the Inner Magnetosphere: A Global MHD and Test-Particle Study
item.description:
Wednesday, July 29, 2026 at 7 PM

Location: Herman Brown Hall

  Speaker: Yiwen Zhu Doctoral Candidate Thesis Defense Department: Physics & Astronomy Location: Herman Brown Hall HBH 254 During geomagnetic storms, ionospheric oxygen (O⁺) can become a significant constituent of Earth's inner magnetosphere, whose storm-time particle buildup drives the main-phase depression of the surface magnetic field. The ionosphere supplies this oxygen from two main regions: the dayside polar cusp and the nightside auroral oval. Their relative contribution to the inner magnetosphere, and how each population is energized as it moves inward, remain poorly quantified, in part because the transport spans scales that no single model resolves. In this thesis, we follow ionospheric oxygen from both sources to the inner magnetosphere using a global magnetohydrodynamic simulation (GAMERA/MAGE) coupled one-way to a test-particle tracer (CHIMP). Because MAGE couples models spanning a range of scales and regions, it resolves both the mesoscale bursty bulk flows (BBFs) of the plasma sheet that drive earthward transport and the particle dynamics of the inner magnetosphere. For a real storm, we compare how cusp and nightside-auroral oxygen reach the plasma sheet and the inner magnetosphere. Within an adiabatic (guiding-center) framework, we decompose the energy gain along the transport into its Fermi, betatron, and E×B contributions and quantify each, and we characterize where the oxygen departs from adiabatic behavior. The two sources follow different paths: cusp oxygen takes the long route through the lobe, while auroral oxygen enters the closed plasma sheet more directly. We also identify a drop-down channel, in which mesoscale plasma-sheet flows pull cusp oxygen down to the equatorial plasma sheet and let it enter the inner magnetosphere more efficiently. To place the contribution on a quantitative footing, we weight the test particles by O⁺ outflow fluences computed directly from the simulation's MHD variables, include charge-exchange loss, and compare the modeled oxygen against Van Allen Probes observations. Cusp oxygen enters the inner magnetosphere at higher energy and auroral oxygen at lower energy, so their relative contribution depends on the number density of ions each source delivers. Through two different storms, we show two cases in which the delivered numbers differ, giving different relative and absolute contributions of the two sources to the inner magnetosphere. Finally, we return to the cusp itself. Predicting where the cusp lies from the upstream solar wind is operationally useful. We develop a machine-learning model, gradient-boosted decision trees trained on DMSP spacecraft cusp crossings, that predicts the cusp location from solar-wind and interplanetary-magnetic-field conditions, offering a fast alternative to a full simulation. Together, these chapters connect the ionospheric sources of inner-magnetosphere oxygen to its delivery and energization: how cusp and auroral O⁺ reach the inner magnetosphere, how each is energized along the way, and how much each contributes across storms. The cusp machine-learning model complements this with a fast predictor of the cusp location from the upstream solar wind. Join via Zoom: https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/97738620987?pwd=OmGDYN5xMiERaeLkGnHvTsx6K0IIOF.1 (https://riceuniversity.zoom.us/j/97738620987?pwd=OmGDYN5xMiERaeLkGnHvTsx6K0IIOF.1) (Department : Physics & Astronomy)

item.title: NASA Stories at the Ion: Building the Moon Base: Challenges and Opportunities at the Lunar South Pole
item.description:
Thursday, July 30, 2026 at 8:30 AM

Location: Ion – Forum Stairs, 4201 Main St., Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Building the Moon Base: Challenges and Opportunities at the Lunar South Pole In this presentation, Moon Base Principal Systems Engineer Shatel Bhakta shares the many challenges NASA must overcome to realize an enduring presence in the lunar South Pole region. He’ll also talk about his journey at NASA, the importance of human space exploration, and what NASA needs from the next generation of aerospace engineers. About the Speaker Shatel Bhakta serves as the principal systems engineer for NASA’s Moon Base. In that role, he takes a system-of-systems view of Moon Base infrastructure, ensuring that all components work together to support NASA’s goal of an enduring human presence in the lunar South Pole region. Prior to working on the Moon Base, Bhakta served as NASA’s lunar architecture lead, guiding a multidisciplinary team across NASA centers to develop a roadmap for crewed exploration of the Moon. This included developing associated conceptual reference missions, concept of operations, site planning guidance, trades and analysis, system element conceptualization, and system-of-systems integration. Bhakta earned his undergraduate degree in mechanical engineering from The University of Texas at Austin and his graduate degree in space architecture from the University of Houston. He is a licensed professional engineer in the state of Texas.  

From Ion District

item.title: Houston Restaurant Weeks 2026
item.description:
Saturday, August 1, 2026 at 12 AM

Houston Restaurant Weeks is the largest annual fundraiser for America’s largest food bank, the Houston Food Bank. It’s a month-long dining extravaganza featuring specially priced lunches, brunches, and dinners at restaurants from The Woodlands to Galveston. Participating restaurants make donations based on how many prix fixe brunches, lunches, and dinners they sell during the event. Diners are not solicited for donations. Beginning July 15, diners can visit HoustonRestaurantWeeks.com to view the 2026 list of restaurants that have committed to participate, along with their HRW menus. The event includes restaurants located in Harris, Galveston, and Montgomery counties. The Galveston County Food Bank and Montgomery County Food Bank are part of the Houston Food Bank’s Affiliate Food Banks. The Houston Food Bank provides food to these smaller food banks, which in turn distribute the food to hunger relief charities in a portion of HFB’s service area. The Houston Food Bank certifies that their Affiliate Food Banks meet Feeding America standards.

item.title: Houston Comic Exchange II
item.description:
Saturday, August 1, 2026 at 10 AM

Houston Comic Exchange II – Built for Comic Collectors Summer is prime comic-hunting season, and CCS Houston Comic Exchange II brings together collectors, dealers, and fans for a day of buying, selling, trading, and discovering comics. From key issues and first appearances to hidden gems and box-fresh finds, every table offers something worth digging for. No gatekeeping, no pressure, just comics and the people who love them.   📅 Saturday, August 1, 2026 | 10AM – 5PM 📍 9700 Bissonnet St, Unit 1500, Houston, TX 🎟️ FREE Entry + FREE Parking   🔥 Event Highlights 🔥 📦 50 Vendor Tables – All Comics, All Formats Singles, back issues, key issues, first appearances, graded slabs, raw runs, indie and small press, variant covers. Vendor tables dedicated entirely to comics, no toys, no filler. If you’re a comic collector, this floor was built for you.   🔍 Key Issues and First Appearances This is where the hunt lives. Vendors bring the deep cuts, raw back issues worth digging through, graded books if you’re chasing condition, and the kind of keys that actually show up when serious collectors are clearing their own collections to make room.   📚 Back-Issue Digging and Indie Discovery Not every great find is a grail. Long boxes of back issues across decades and publishers, plus indie comics and small press titles that never make it to a standard shop shelf. Come with a list or come ready to browse – both work.   🤝 Vendors Who Collect Too The people behind these tables are the same people who will ask what you’re hunting before they start pulling books for you. The Houston Comic Exchange is a community floor first. The conversations are part of the event.   🛒 Vendor Table Applications Houston comic vendors: we’re gathering a focused comics-only crowd, and free entry is driving serious foot traffic. Apply for your table here 👉🏻 https://forms.gle/7q6pjcoiJTPbJouP8   The key issue you’ve been tracking is probably in one of those long boxes this summer. The Houston Comic Exchange II, August 1. Free entry, free parking, always.

From CCS Houston

item.title: Houston Toy Exchange III
item.description:
Sunday, August 2, 2026 at 5 AM

Houston Toy Exchange III — The Floor Is Loaded, Houston Somewhere on this floor is the piece you have been hunting for months. 🔥 Houston Toy Exchange III is a pure toy marketplace, no convention noise, no filler. Just collectors, families, and dealers moving action figures, vintage finds, and modern grails across one packed floor at CCS Houston. The fun is in the hunt: digging through a bin you have never seen, talking shop with someone who knows the line better than you do, and walking out with something you did not expect to find.   📅 Date: Sunday, August 2, 2026 | 10AM – 5PM 📍 Location: 9700 Bissonnet St, #1500, Houston, TX 77036 🎟️ FREE Entry + FREE Parking   🔥 What You’ll Find on the Floor 🔥 🛍️ Toy Marketplace Tables packed with action figures, vintage toys, sealed and loose, nostalgia pieces, and the modern lines collectors are actually chasing right now. Every table is its own dig. Come search the floor.   💰 Buy, Sell, Trade Bring the toys you are ready to pass along or trade up for something you have been chasing. Collectors and vendors are buying, selling, and trading all day. Connect, negotiate, and keep great pieces moving through the community.   🔍 Toy Appraisals Holding something and not sure what it’s worth? One of our experienced vendors is running toy appraisals all day, sharing insights on value, rarity, and trade potential so you can make confident, informed deals on the floor.   🧩 Toy Scavenger Hunt Challenge Turn the hunt into a game. Work the marketplace and complete the Toy Hunt Challenge by tracking down specific toy categories across multiple booths for a shot at prizes and collector bragging rights.   📸 Toy Flex Wall Score something special? Show it off. Snap a photo of your best pickup at the Toy Flex Wall and share your find with the community.   Longtime collector or just starting out, Houston Toy Exchange III is about connecting, swapping stories, and keeping the love of toys alive together. Bring your toys, bring your curiosity, pull up.   Want in as a vendor? Tables are open: https://tinyurl.com/CCSGuestVendorFromHouston   Houston Toy Exchange III. Bring your toys, bring your curiosity, and come move some pieces.

From CCS Houston

item.title: Jesus Benavente: NUESTROWORLD
item.description:
Thursday, August 13, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: DiverseWorks, @ 5601 B Navigation Blvd & Various Locations, 5601 B Navigation Blvd, Houston, TX, 77011, United States

Jesus Benavente, A life, A Home and A Horse Named Triste, 2021, courtesy of the artist. Opening Thursday, August 13, 2026 | 6 – 8 PM Gallery Hours: Thurs – Sat 12 – 6 PM NUESTROWORLD is a satirical solo exhibition by Brooklyn-based artist Jesus Benavente, conceived of as a visual album and immersive “amusement park.” This project features interconnected works unfolding across the gallery and city, collectively highlighting Houston’s cyclical history of ambition, folly, and heartbreak. The title NUESTROWORLD is a play on Astroworld and uses Spanglish to create the phrase “The World Is Ours.” The project draws inspiration from popular events that mark specific eras of Houston’s history, such as the opening of the world-famous Astrodome and Astroworld Park in the late 60’s, Selena’s iconic Rodeo performances in the 90’s, and the folklore surrounding the 1836 capture of Santa Anna during the Battle of San Jacinto as part of the Texas Revolution. Together, they build a story, a world developed over time that underscores sacrifice, instills resilience, and highlights a Texas attitude of “come and take it.”  ARTIST BIO: Jesus Benavente is a visual artist based in Brooklyn, New York. Jesus earned an MFA from Rutgers University and attended Skowhegan School of Painting and Sculpture. Recent exhibitions and performances include the Whitney Museum of American Art, New York; Queens Museum, Queens; LTD Los Angeles, Los Angeles; Performa 13, New York; Acre Projects, Chicago; Chinati Foundation, Marfa; the Neuberger Museum of Art, Purchase, NY; Shin Museum of Art, South Korea; Vox Populi, Philadelphia; Socrates Sculpture Park, New York; and Austin Museum of Art. Benavente was born in San Antonio, Texas.  

From DiverseWorks

item.title: Retro Video Game Expo III
item.description:
Saturday, August 15, 2026 at 10 AM

🕹️ Houston, Press Start on a Weekend of Pure Retro Nostalgia! 👾 Step back into the golden era of gaming at Retro Video Game Expo III, a two-day celebration of classic consoles, arcade legends, competitive retro tournaments, and nonstop free play. From expanded free-play zones spanning the 80s and beyond to live, high-energy tournament matchups and a collector-focused marketplace, this expo is built for gamers who chase high scores and grail finds.   🗓️ Date & Time: August 15–16, 2026 | 10AM–5PM 📍 Location: 9700 Bissonnet St #1500, Houston, TX 77036 💥 FREE ENTRY. FREE PARKING. FREE PLAY. 🎮 Event Highlights 🎮 Retro Video Game Marketplace – All Weekend Step into a collector’s paradise. Vendors from across the region are bringing vintage consoles, original cartridges, imports, manuals, accessories, and hard-to-find titles. This is where treasures respawn. 🚨 Want to vend? Sign up here 👉 https://tinyurl.com/HoustonVendors   🎮 Free-Play Zone – ALL Day Jump on 80’s Arcades & Classic Consoles and relive the games that made gaming legendary. More setups and activities to be announced soon! 🤝 Calling All Collaborators & Retro Communities This event is built with the community for community! We’re actively looking to partner with: 🏁 Tournament organizers → https://forms.gle/74Qvuv9PFzeDVF1V8 🕹️ Pinball/Arcade Hosts → https://forms.gle/74Qvuv9PFzeDVF1V8 🎤 Workshops & Panels → https://forms.gle/q2nCKsZ6FEVZBgqW9 🙌 Volunteer Sign-Up → https://forms.gle/15zMGTqZPSGKjGdy6 🎮 Vendor Applications → https://tinyurl.com/CCSGuestVendorFromHouston If you’ve ever wanted to be part of event, bring your passion! Let’s chat! 📩   🏨 Special Hotel Deals Enjoy a special rate of $79/night — 2 Queens at TownePlace Suites, only 15 minutes distance from the action! Book your stay 👉🏻 https://www.marriott.com/event-reservations/reservation-link.mi?id=1767823967549&key=CORP&app=resvlink   Bring your crew, grab a controller, and let’s relive the golden age of gaming together. 👾✨

item.title: Froggy Night
item.description:
Saturday, August 15, 2026 at 7 PM

$37 member / $52 nonmemberInstructor: Dr. Cassidy Johnson Ages 21+ Hop on over for a wet, wild night! Enjoy refreshments (frog-themed snacks, coffee, and Saint Arnold Brewing Company beer) while you learn all about the strange and wonderful world of frogs, from their croaking courtship to their mysterious metamorphosis. Weather permitting, we’ll also go for a hike to search for frogs and other nocturnal creatures. Please dress for the weather and wear walking shoes. register online Instructor bio: Dr. Cassidy Johnson has a B.S. and M.S. in Biology at Texas A&M University – Corpus Christi and a Ph.D. in Biochemistry & Cell Biology from Rice University. She loves teaching biology and is currently an Assistant Teaching Professor for Rice BioSciences. She fell in love with local amphibians while working for the Houston toad ex situ conservation program at the Houston Zoo. She is also passionate about the protection and restoration of Texas prairies and is on the board of the Native Prairie Association of Texas and was previously the president of the Coastal Prairie Partnership.

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.title: Docent Recruitment Open House & Breakfast
item.description:
Thursday, August 20, 2026 at 10 AM

FreeRegistration encouraged; walk-in participants welcomeAges 21+ Calling all nature lovers! We are looking to grow our team of Arboretum Docents and would like to invite you to learn more at this informational breakfast. Docents are volunteers who are specially trained to engage visitors of all ages and backgrounds in active explorations of our trails and Discovery Room. We are currently recruiting individuals for our upcoming docent trainings to prepare for fall programs! RSVP Online Concerned that you know very little about natural history, native flora/fauna, or the Arboretum in general? Not to worry! Docent training is comprehensive and includes extensive content-based classes as well as training on effective touring techniques. If you are interested in helping us teach our visitors about nature and all it has to offer, we encourage you to attend!

item.title: Fourth Saturday Phenology Walk
item.description:
Saturday, August 22, 2026 at 9 AM

Fourth Saturday of the Month9:00 – 11:00 amFree, donations appreciatedAll ages, minors must be accompanied by an adult Meet in front of the Nature Center building Discover the hidden seasonal rhythms of nature firsthand on our guided Phenology Walks, where we track the life cycles of different plants across ecosystems, from the first spring bud burst to winter dormancy. You’ll learn how shifting weather patterns and climate change influence the timing of these important events in our local ecosystems and how you can become a community scientist, contributing vital data from your own backyard to a global research initiative. These relaxing morning walks are led by scientists from Rice University and staff from the Arboretum. We welcome nature enthusiasts of all ages, however kids 12 years and younger must be accompanied by a guardian. Learn more about the study of phenology and ways you can contribute at https://www.usanpn.org/nn Community Science Partner

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.description:

$22 member / $37 nonmemberAges 12+, minors must be accompanied by an adult What’s the best time to plant wildflowers, put up a birdhouse, or clean up the garden after a freeze? With a little understanding of nature’s rhythms, you can plan your year to maximize wildlife benefits and minimize your stress. In this class we’ll talk through a year in the wildlife garden and send you home with a calendar of to-dos for each season. Please dress for the weather and wear walking shoes. register online

item.title: Author Talk with Dr. Pamela Toler, Author of The Dragon From Chicago
item.description:
Thursday, August 27, 2026 at 6:30 PM

Location: Albert and Ethel Herzstein Theater on the Mady and Ken Kades Stage

Join Holocaust Museum Houston for a night with Dr. Pamela Toler, Author of The Dragon from Chicago: The Untold Story of an American Reporter in Nazi Germany.      “Today we face an alarming upsurge in the spread of misinformation and attempts by powerful figures to discredit facts so they can seize control of our political and cultural narratives. These are threats American journalist Sigrid Schultz knew all too well. The Chicago Tribune’s Berlin bureau chief and primary foreign correspondent for Central Europe from 1925 to January 1941, Schultz witnessed Hitler’s rise to power and was one of the first reporters—male or female—to warn American readers of the growing dangers of Nazism.  She was one of the last to leave Berlin before it was too late.     In The Dragon From Chicago, historian Pamela Toler tells the story of Schultz’s years spent courageously reporting the news from Berlin, from the revolts of 1919 through the Nazi rise to power and Allied air raids over Berlin in 1941. At a time when women reporters rarely wrote front-page stories, Schultz regularly  reported the truth about Nazi Germany in the face of censorship and the threat of expulsion, internment, or death. The Nazis called Schultz “that dragon from Chicago.” One of her fellow correspondents called her “Adolph Hitler’s greatest enemy.” Schultz herself claimed to be “just a reporter.” Her story is a powerful account of one woman standing up for truth in an era marked by the spread of disinformation and propaganda spawned by hate.”     Books will be available for purchase by credit card.

From Holocaust Museum Houston

item.title: Triple Crown Celebration
item.description:
Thursday, August 27, 2026 at 9 PM

Location: Duncan Hall

Join us in honoring Lydia Kavraki (https://news.rice.edu/news/2025/national-academy-sciences-elects-lydia-kavraki-member) and Rebecca Richards-Kortum (https://news.rice.edu/news/2025/richards-kortum-elected-national-academy-medicine), two scholars whose careers exemplify the highest ideals of research, innovation, mentorship and service. Through groundbreaking discoveries, commitment to students, and work that has improved lives around the world, they have advanced their fields and inspired the next generation of researchers, engineers and scientists. They are also the only two researchers in Texas elected to all three National Academies, an extraordinary distinction held by fewer than 35 living researchers nationwide. The program will feature reflections from university leadership, perspectives from colleagues, and a conversation with the honorees on the work, values and experiences that have shaped their remarkable careers.RSVP for this special event! CCS Card Show I — Every Sport. Every TCG. One Floor. Houston, the hobby comes home. For the first time at CCS, every major sport and every major TCG land under one roof: sports card collectors, memorabilia hunters, and TCG players moving cards on the same floor, the way it should be. item.title: Rice360 Global Health Technologies Seminar Series: AI Driven Wearable Sensors for Maternal and Newborn Health in Low Resource Settings
item.description:
Tuesday, September 1, 2026 at 10 PM

Location: BioScience Research Collaborative

Join Rice360 for engaging conversations with leaders in global health and development as they share their expert insights on the intersection of medicine, technology and policy. Steve Xu, MD, MSc is a physician-engineer, entrepreneur, and board-certified dermatologist. He is the CEO and co-founder of Sibel Health as well as the Ruth K. Freinkel, MD Professor at Northwestern University. He received his undergraduate degree in bioengineering from Rice University summa cum laude, an MD from Harvard Medical School (Soros Fellow), and a Masters in Health Policy from The London School of Economics (Marshall Scholar). Dr. Xu has authored more than 120 peer-reviewed publications and listed as an inventor on 15 pending and granted patents. As both an NIH, Gates Foundation, FDA, and DoD funded investigator, he has led complex engineering, artificial intelligence, and clinical development efforts worldwide. As an MIT 35 Under 35 Technology innovator, his publications have appeared in Nature, Science, The Proceedings of the National Academy of Medicine, and the New England Journal of Medicine garnering press attention from The New York Times, CNN, The Washington Post, and The Los Angeles Times. Within 4 years of founding, Sibel Health has obtained six FDA 510(k) clearances, monitored more than 16,000 individuals, and launched in more than 20 countries worldwide with its ICU-grade wearable sensors for maternal neonatal health.

From Rice University - Open to the Public

Event details

item.title: Edible Wild Plants
item.description:
Sunday, September 6, 2026 at 1 PM

$100 member / $125 nonmember (per person)Ages 16+, minors must be accompanied by an adult For most of human existence, the wilds supplied all our food and medicine. Join Dr. Mark “Merriwether” Vorderbruggen as he teaches you what your ancestors knew. This plant walkabout will give you hands-on (as well as nose, fingers, and taste bud) guidance on how to properly identify and utilize the wonderful wild plants of the Houston/East Texas region. Please dress for the weather and wear walking shoes. register online Instructor bio: Dr. Mark Vorderbruggen brings his background as a Ph.D. in chemistry to the world of Houston’s edible and medicinal wild plants. He is the author of “The Idiot’s Guide: Foraging,” runs the informative “Foraging Texas” website, formulates medicinal plant remedies through Medicine Man Plant Co., and is always educating about useful plants on TV, online, and in person.

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

Event details

item.title: Discover Nature Together Scavenger Hunts
item.description:
Sunday, September 6, 2026 at 2 PM

Free, donations appreciatedAll ages, minors must be accompanied by an adult Bring the whole family to the Houston Arboretum for free, themed scavenger hunts! Each month features a themed self-guided scavenger hunt where families can join us at our Nature Center before heading out to the trails to sharpen their observation skills and learn something new about nature. From spiders to fall foliage, every adventure is different! Please come prepared for the outdoors (closed toe shoes recommended, bring a water bottle, bug spray, etc).  Signs of LifeSeptember 6 We may not always see animals out and about, so how do we know they are here? They leave traces of themselves behind! From scat, to tracks, learn how to find the signs of life here at the Arboretum. Amazing ArachnidsOctober 10 Spiders are so much more than Halloween decorations. They fill the role of pest control specialist in our ecosystem. Want to learn more about these amazing arachnids? Then get into the Halloween spirit by learning more about spiders. Fall FoliageNovember 7 Although Houston is not known for its fall colors, there are still lots to learn about leaves! From deciduous to evergreen, here at the Arboretum we see leaves on the ground as well as in the trees all winter long. Join us and learn more about the difference between the two and why leaves are important in the fall. Animal HomesDecember 5 There is no central heating outdoors, so where do the animals go when they get cold? To their homes, of course! Burrows, leaves, nests, and so much more. Find out all the different types of animal homes and who lives in what.

From Houston Arboretum & Nature Center

item.title: SynthX "Unlocking the Clinical Potential of Chemical Innovation" Workshop
item.description:
Tuesday, September 8, 2026 at 5 PM

Location: BioScience Research Collaborative

By harnessing the expertise and resources of various groups within the TMC, this long-term series aims to bridge the gap between biomedical innovations and clinical applications, offering valuable insights to researchers from Rice and the TMC regarding biomedical challenges and potential solutions. Faculty, postdocs, students, and other researchers are invited to attend. Lunch is provided. — Prof. Lingyan Shi and her team are developing and applying new ultrafast laser scanning multimodal imaging and spectroscopic technologies, such as stimulated Raman scattering (SRS), DO-SRS, second harmonic generation (SHG), Fluorescence Lifetime Imaigng (FLIM), and multiphoton fluorescence (MPF) microscopy, for visualizing molecular events and metabolic dynamics in situ at subcellular resolution for studying aging and diseases. Prof. Shi and her team discovered "Golden Window" (from 1550nm to 1870nm) wavelength for deep optical tissue imaging (Shi et al., 2016), established PRM (Zhang et al., 2024) SRS and A-POD (Jang et al., 2023) super resolution multi-molecular imaging platform. Shi Lab is developing and applying bioorthogonal SRS imaging methods for dissecting complex cellular machinery in living organisms during aging processes and disease progression, offering powerful tools potentially for diagnosis, assessing therapeutic efficacy/resistance, as well as for mechanistic understanding of scientific fundamentals in neurodegenerative diseases, cancer, drug discovery, and aging processes.

From Rice University - Open to the Public

item.title: The Music Man
item.description:
Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 8 AM

Location: The Hobby Center, 800 Bagby St, Houston, TX 77002, United States, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

Seventy-six trombones. One unforgettable musical! Meredith Willson’s six-time Tony Award®-winning beloved musical comedy The Music Man marches into Houston with laughter, heart, and all the music you love. Following the fast-talking traveling salesman Harold Hill as he cons the people of River City, Iowa, into buying instruments and uniforms for a boys’ band that he vows to organize. Featuring songs such as “Seventy-Six Trombones,” “Trouble,” “’Till There Was You,” “Pick-a-Little,” and “Gary, Indiana,” The Music Man is a classic musical to be shared with every generation. CRITICAL ACCLAIM FOR THE MUSIC MAN – The Telegraph “A joyous, blissful Broadway event!” – Variety “Grand and Glorious!” “…totally enchanting abso-tootin’-lutely smashing revival. It will give you new life.” PERFORMANCE SCHEDULE Tuesday, Sept 15, 7:30 p.m. – H-E-B Community Night Wednesday, Sept 16, 7:30 p.m. Thursday, Sept 17, 7:30 p.m. Friday, Sept 18, 8 p.m. Saturday, Sept 19, 2 p.m. Saturday, Sept 19, 8 p.m. Sunday, Sept 20, 2 p.m. Sunday, Sept 20, 7:30 p.m. Tuesday, Sept 22, 7:30 p.m. Wednesday, Sept 23, 7:30 p.m. Thursday, Sept 24, 7:30 p.m. Friday, Sept 25, 8 p.m. Saturday, Sept 26, 2 p.m. — Open Captioned Saturday, Sept 26, 8 p.m. Sunday, Sept 27, 2 p.m. — ASL & Audio Described SUBSCRIBE NOW TICKETING INFO Season tickets are now available. 6-show packages start at just $34 per-show. Tickets are $46 and are available online or by calling TUTS Guest Services at 713-558-8887. Tickets will also available in person Monday through Friday from Noon to 6 p.m. at the TUTS Box Office, located in the Hobby Center lobby. Discounted group tickets are available for parties of 10 or more.Theatre Under The Stars has a variety of accessibility options for guests.Learn more about accessible performances and other services here. Rush tickets will be available for $35 at the box office for mezzanine and gallery seating starting 2 hours prior to curtain. Questions about parking, dining or other aspects of attending a TUTS show? We’ve got answers! RUN TIME 2 hours and 30 minutes including intermission Photos Photos by Marshall Meadows VIDEOS CREATIVE TEAM Matt Lenz Director Joshua Bergasse Choreographer Ann Beyersdorfer Set Designer Santo Loquasto Original Broadway and Tour Costume Designer Ken Billington Lighting Designer Lisa Renkel Video & Projection Designer Walter Trarbach Sound Designer Roxanne De Luna Wig & Makeup Designer Robin L. item.title: Unified Topgolf Pro-Am (Houston-Katy)
item.description:
Friday, September 18, 2026 at 10 AM

Location: Topgolf-Katy, 1030 Memorial Brook Blvd, Houston, TX 77084, Houston, 77084

The Unified Topgolf Pro-Am is one of the most exciting and meaningful community partnership events hosted by Special Olympics Texas, bringing together athletes, families, coaches, volunteers, corporate partners, and local business leaders for an unforgettable day of golf, laughter, connection, and community impact. Each bay includes a Special Olympics Texas athlete paired alongside five golfers, creating a truly unique experience where relationships, memories, and meaningful moments are built throughout the day. From friendly competition and team spirit to incredible conversations and shared experiences, the event is designed to bring people together in a fun and welcoming environment while directly supporting local athletes and programs. Proceeds from the Unified Topgolf Pro-Am help provide year-round sports training, competitions, health initiatives, leadership development, and educational opportunities for children, teenagers, and adults with intellectual disabilities throughout the greater Houston area. As the event continues growing each year, the Unified Topgolf Pro-Am has quickly become a tremendous opportunity for organizations and community members to make a real impact while being part of something incredibly energetic, uplifting, and memorable. For more information regarding sponsorship opportunities, team entries, volunteer involvement, or sponsorship opportunities, please reach out to Jared Kossover, Strategic Partnerships Manager with Special Olympics Texas Jared Kossover E: jkossover@sotx.org C: 737-867-9659

item.title: Demon Slayer Mini Con
item.description:
Saturday, September 19, 2026 at 10 AM

🔥 Calling all Demon Slayer Corps members, Hashira-in-training, and Tanjiro fans**!** 🔥 From Mizunoto beginners to seasoned Hashira, masters of Sun Breathing to the loyal members of the Zenitsu-squad, Demon Slayer Mini Con is your next mission! CCS Houston is hosting a one-day Total Concentration event for every slayer who lives for the Hinokami Kagura, the intensity of the Upper Rank battles, and the bond between friends. Join the Corps for a day packed with Nichirin-grade marketplace finds, Cosplay haoris, and Blood Demon Art energy, all in a fan-first space where no one is left in the Final Selection alone. Steel your heart, grab your Kasugai Crow, and let’s set our hearts ablaze together ⚔️✨   🗓️ Date & Time: Saturday, Sept 19, 2026 | 10AM – 5PM 📍 Location: 9700 Bissonnet St, #1500, Houston, TX 77036 🎟️ FREE Entry + FREE Parking   👘 Demon Slayer Cosplay Showcase + Demon Face-Off (2 PM) Prepare for a Hashira-level showdown in a dramatic pose-off against our “demon.” The crowd’s roar will determine who survives the night and claims victory.   🎴 Nichirin Sword Pose-Off (3PM) Even without a uniform, your spirit can burn bright! Grab a Nichirin blade, take the stage, and unleash your most iconic Breathing Style pose for a chance to win a prize.   🎮 Demon Slayer: Hinokami Chronicles Free-Play Zone (All Day) Jump into the action in our gaming area! Join free play sessions on the Demon Slayer: The Hinokami Chronicles video game and challenge fellow slayers to a dueling trial.   Demon Slayer Trivia (3:30 PM) Only those with the sharpest focus will survive this mental trial and earn their rank as a true scholar of the series.   🎨 Nezuko’s Box DIY Craft Station (All Day) Channel your inner Urokodaki to construct a miniature wooden-style carrier using paper, charms, and markers. Open to all ages!   🔥 Demon Slayer Artist Alley Wander through a marketplace filled with hand-forged treasures and fandom collectibles, including custom Nichirin charms, Demon Slayer-inspired prints, and talismans for the next mission, our Artist Alley features the most talented creators in the Corps. 🔥 Want to create something special for Demon Slayer fans? 🔗 Host activities, workshops, or panels → https://forms.gle/q2nCKsZ6FEVZBgqW9 🔗 Volunteer Sign-Up → https://forms.gle/15zMGTqZPSGKjGdy6 🔗 Vendor Applications → https://tinyurl.com/HoustonVendors

Looking for the ultimate Houston drag brunch experience? Whether you're planning a bachelorette party, a birthday celebration, or just want a daytime drag show without the late-night crowd, this is your event. Drag Brunch at The Punch is a monthly extravaganza featuring fierce performances, sassy audience games, and unforgettable live drag performances ? paired with brunch cocktails, mimosas, and bites. The perfect daytime LGBTQ event for anyone who loves fabulous entertainment before sundown. Produced by RuPaul's Drag Race fan-favorite Cynthia Lee Fontaine, each show features Houston drag queens bringing show-stopping numbers, big laughs, and serious talent. Perfect for girls' day out, gay brunch, Pride celebrations, and anyone looking for a fun Saturday activity in Houston. Floyd Distinguished Professor of Engineering at UC Berkeley and President of the Robot Learning Foundation Talk Title: TBD When: Thursday, September 24, 2026 @ 4:00-6:00 PM Central Where: Auditorium, Duncan Hall, Rice University (6100 Main St., Houston, TX 77005) Parking: Paid parking will be available in Founder's Court Lot or the Entrance 3 (COB) Garage. Floyd Distinguished Professor of Engineering at UC Berkeley, President of the international Robot Learning Foundation, IEEE Fellow, co-founder and Editor-in-Chief emeritus of the IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering (T-ASE), and Co-Founder/Chief Scientist of Ambi Robotics. Ken leads research in robotics and automation: grasping, manipulation, and learning for applications in warehouses, homes, agriculture, and robot-assisted surgery. He is Distinguished Professor of IEOR, EECS, and Art Practice. Ken has published 12 US patents and over 450 refereed papers. He has presented over 600 invited lectures to academic and corporate audiences.

item.title: OVERFLOW RADIO: Šakotayišol Nunuš Constellation
item.description:
Saturday, October 3, 2026 at 12 AM

Location: DiverseWorks – Gallery @ MATCH, 3400 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002, United States

October 3-24, 2026DiverseWorks Gallery @ MATCHGallery Hours: 12 noon – 6 pm, Thursday-Saturday Celebrated for her large-scale social choreographies, Emily Johnson / Catalyst’s newest project, Overflow Radio is a performance, skill-share, planting of 1000 trees, and radio transmission from across territories. In conjunction with the world premiere of Overflow Radio in Mni Sóta Makoce (Minneapolis), DiverseWorks hosts an Overflow Radio: Šakotayišol Nunuš Constellation here in Houston. Over 24 non-consecutive hours, we will gather in-person to listen to twelve First Nations and Indigenous authors, poets, and scholars live-broadcasting from their home territories and First Nations. We’ll pay attention to other scales, other forms, other knowledges. We’ll traverse together, transcending colonial borders, languages and time. We’ll feast and celebrate the making of community, as we practice our shared commitment to creating our possible futures, as we gather what we need to know. The program is developed in collaboration with Emily Johnson and local Indigenous and Native artists to include talks, skill-shares, listening gatherings, an exhibition, and performances by Aveda Adara, Chiara Beaumont, ChiChi, Karen Navarro, Aryn Ward and Monica Villarreal, with additional participating artists and community partners to be announced. The project is co-organized by DiverseWorks, Emily Johnson / Catalyst and the participating artists and partners. Programs (please check back for updated information)DW Art + Climate CONVERSATIONS: Emily Johnson, 6:30 pm July 29Opening Event and Reception: 5 – 8 pm, October 3Listening Gatherings: 12noon – 6 pm (specific hours TBD), October 9-12Diverse Discourse Lecture & Studio Visits: Mary Bourdeaux: October 16-19 / Lecture 6 pm, Oct. 17Closing Event: TBD, October 24 AcknowledgementsOverflow Radio is a National Performance Network Creation & Development Fund Project commissioned by Roy and Edna Disney / CalArts Theater (REDCAT) and co-commissioned DiverseWorks, MASS MoCA and University of Minnesota Department of Theatre Arts & Dance, more information at www.npnweb.org. Overflow Radio is developed through creative residencies provided by MASS MoCA, John and Mabel Ringling Museum of Art, Roy and Edna Disney / CalArts Theater, University of Minnesota’s Imagine Fund with support from the McKnight Foundation, and Danspace Project with support from the New York State DanceForce, a partnership program of the New York State Council on the Arts. Overflow Radio is created with generous support from First Peoples Fund, Howard Gilman Foundation, Harkness Foundation for Dance, and the New England Foundation for the Arts’ National Dance Project with lead funding from the Doris Duke Foundation and The Mellon Foundation. Emily Johnson / Catalyst is fiscally sponsored by Producer Hub. Image: Emily Johnson / Catalyst, Quilt Being Star, worn by Ty Fierce Matteba, photo by Two Hawks Young.

From DiverseWorks
